nodes.plm_action: Applying strips in correct order
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a tutorial demonstrating how to create a wallet out of duct tape.

summary.brief: A step‑by‑step tutorial shows how to cut, fold, and tri‑weave colored duct‑tape strips to create a multi‑colored wallet.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the presenter greeting viewers for “Weaving Wednesday” and listing the supplies: three colors of duct tape, a metal ruler, an X‑Acto knife, and clear tape. Strips of each color are measured and cut – 8‑inch pieces are halved and then each half is folded back on itself to make a rounded edge, while a 9‑inch length is cut into thirds for each color and then each third is halved and folded the same way. An 8‑inch strip designated as the trim is also cut in half. The folded 3‑inch strips are aligned on a yellow grid mat and attached to the trim piece at about a quarter‑inch interval, forming a base strip. The presenter then weaves the three colors together by laying the first color over one strip, under the next, and repeating this over‑under pattern across the whole length; the second and third colors are woven in the same alternating fashion, creating the tri‑color effect. After the weave is complete, clear tape is applied to the back, and the sides are taped along the top edge. The excess edge is trimmed with a ruler to about a quarter of an inch, then folded inward so the woven panel has a rounded outer edge. This finished tri‑weave panel is attached to the main wallet body, the seam is trimmed, and the final wallet is displayed, with the presenter counting the colored squares and showing the wallet from several angles before signing off.

action.detailed: Cut the duct‑tape into measured strips, fold each strip to form a rounded edge, arrange the strips on the mat and attach them to a trim piece, then weave the three colors together in an over‑under pattern, tape the back and sides, trim and fold the edge to round it, attach the woven panel to the wallet body, and finally display the finished wallet.

nodes.plm_action: Taping 2 lines to complete the wallet
nodes.plm_caption:
In this video, a person is showcasing their duct tape wallet. They cut some red and white tape into strips and stick them to their wallet. They cut it into different shapes before sticking it to their wallet. They finish by sticking the top of the wallet together. The person's hands move quickly and the background is not visible.
The person is wearing no distinguishable item. It is very dark with no lighting on it. The person is using a silver ruler, a pen and white, red, and black tape on it. The wallet was placed on a yellow, checkered surface.
There are no other objects in the video. The surface that the person is cutting their tape on has visible marking, grids and numbers.

summary.brief: A tutorial shows how to cut, fold, and weave three colors of duct‑tape into a tri‑weave panel that is then attached to a duct‑tape wallet.
summary.detailed: The video begins with an introduction to “Weaving Wednesday” and a list of supplies: three colors of duct tape, a metal ruler, an X‑Acto knife, clear tape, and a cutting mat. The creator cuts three 8‑inch strips in half, peels each half and folds it back on itself to form rounded strips, and repeats the same folding with 9‑inch strips that have been divided into thirds and then halved. An 8‑inch strip is cut in half to serve as a trim, and small 3‑inch pieces of tape are glued onto this trim at quarter‑inch intervals. Using an over‑under pattern, the first color (red) is woven across the base, then the second color, then the third, continuing the sequence until the tri‑weave texture appears. Clear tape is applied to the back of the woven panel, the sides are taped, and the edges are trimmed to a quarter‑inch width with the ruler and folded inward to create a rounded edge. Finally, the finished woven panel is attached to the pre‑made duct‑tape wallet, completing the tri‑weave wallet, which is displayed on a yellow‑checkered cutting mat.

action.brief: Weave duct‑tape strips into a tri‑weave wallet
action.detailed: Weave colored duct‑tape strips over and under each other, secure the back and sides with clear tape, trim and fold the edges with a ruler, and attach the woven panel to the wallet to finish the tri‑weave wallet.

nodes.plm_action: Weave duct tape to create pattern
nodes.plm_caption: A video of a person completing a multi-colored wallet with duct tape.

summary.brief: Hands interlace black, red and white tape strips into a tri‑weave panel, attach it to a duct‑tape wallet, and then flip and open the finished wallet to show its pockets.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with the crafter’s hands rapidly laying black, red and white tape strips on a yellow, grid‑lined cutting mat and interlacing them in an over‑under pattern while using a ruler to keep the rows even, trimming and folding the woven panel as needed; the completed tri‑weave piece is then aligned and affixed to the body of the duct‑tape wallet. In the later part of the segment the hands lift the wallet, rotate it, open and close it several times, count the colored squares, and display the interior pockets and the items placed inside.

action.detailed: Weave the black, red, and white duct‑tape strips by interlacing them in an over‑under pattern on the yellow grid mat, trim and fold the woven panel, attach it to the wallet, then open and flip the finished wallet to reveal its pockets.

nodes.plm_action: Cut strips of duct tape using an X-Acto knife
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a timelapse of someone preparing and cutting fabric to create a custom wallet. They first lay out a pre-cut wallet and then proceed to cut small, striped fabric from a larger sheet and lay them out. They then use a pen knife to cut a specific length of fabric and start to attach the fabric to the wallet.

summary.brief: Timelapse of assembling a cardboard wallet and preparing colored duct‑tape strips for a tri‑weave wallet.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a branded logo screen that fades to a white‑grid cutting mat. A quick series of shots then shows various cloth‑style wristbands and patterned red, white and black duct‑tape swatches placed on the yellow, checkered surface. The presenter’s hands pick up two cardboard halves of a wallet, repeatedly open and close them, and insert cardboard pieces to form a basket‑shaped body, displaying both the interior and exterior of the partially built wallet on the yellow table. After this, the focus shifts to the cutting mat where rolls of red, white and black duct‑tape are laid out. Using a metal ruler as a guide, the hands cut long tape strips, cut those into short lengths, and fold each short piece in half lengthwise. The folded strips are aligned side‑by‑side on the mat, separated by the ruler. The strips are then layered onto a piece of paper—first a red strip, followed by white and black strips—each attached with clear tape. The segment ends with the prepared, folded tape strips neatly arranged on the work surface, ready for the weaving stage.

action.detailed: Cut colored duct‑tape into equal short lengths, fold each lengthwise, line the folded strips on the grid mat using a ruler as a guide, and adhere them onto a sheet of paper with clear tape to create the components for a tri‑weave wallet.

nodes.plm_action: Weave tape strips into rectangular box using fingers
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a close up shot of a pair of hands cutting  red and black duct tape on a yellow mat. At the end, the person is arranging these strips on another mat. There is bright and even lighting.

summary.brief: Hands cut, tear and layer red, black and white duct‑tape strips on a yellow‑grid mat to build a multi‑colored strip.
summary.detailed: A pair of hands works over a bright yellow, grid‑lined cutting mat. First a red duct‑tape strip is torn or cut in half, then placed over an existing black‑and‑white strip. The strip is pressed, the partially assembled piece is flipped, and another colored strip (red, black or white) is added from the right side. This sequence of cutting, overlapping, flipping and tucking the ends repeats, gradually extending the tape strip until a layered strip of eight alternating colors is formed. In the final moments the hands adjust the last black strip and align the whole assembly.

action.detailed: Tear or cut each colored duct‑tape strip, place it onto the growing assembly, overlap it with the previous layers, flip the piece as needed, and tuck the ends to secure the pattern.

nodes.plm_action: Placing tape along the edge of the pattern
nodes.plm_caption: A person demonstrates weaving using black, red and white strips. Some of the black and white strips already have been woven. The video speed is high. The video takes place on a flat surface with black lines on it. There is a ruler at the bottom of the screen. It is unclear what material the strips are made of. The person moves the strips quickly to show the process.

summary.brief: Fast‑motion demonstration of weaving black, red, and white strips into a tri‑weave on a ruler‑lined cutting mat.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with the crafter spreading red, white and black strips on a pale‑yellow cutting mat that shows a grid and a ruler along the bottom edge. After briefly folding one strip, both hands pick up the pieces and interlace them over‑and‑under an already‑started black‑and‑white base, extending the tri‑weave pattern while keeping the strips aligned with the ruler. The motion is shown in fast‑forward, making the weaving appear rapid. When the pattern is mostly complete, the hands lift the edge of the partially finished piece, flip it over and make final adjustments to tighten and align the weave, ending with a close‑up of the woven area being inspected and smoothed.

action.detailed: Interlace the red, white, and black strips over and under the existing woven base, aligning them against the ruler on the cutting mat and adjusting the edges to complete the tri‑weave pattern.

nodes.plm_action: Cutting away excess duct tape along marked lines
nodes.plm_caption:
A person makes a small pocket by weaving a piece of paper. The video is in fast motion. The pocket is black, red and white. The person flips the pocket, opens the pocket and shows inside it.
A square piece of paper can be seen first, slightly folded out to make a pocket. It is in three layers: black, red and white. A tool is seen being used in the background on the left and a silver pen is placed to the right. The paper is being folded into a pocket in a weaved pattern. They are using a hand tool.
The cutting mat can be seen below, and the person's left hand is above the paper. In the background a black object is seen on the cutting mat, to the left of the paper. There are no other objects in the background.
The video is in fast motion.

summary.brief: A three‑colored paper piece is woven into a small pocket, flipped, and opened to show its interior.
summary.detailed: On a yellow cutting mat, a square sheet of paper layered in black, red, and white is manipulated with a hand tool and the creator’s left hand. The layers are woven and folded together to form a compact pocket. The pocket is then turned over, its edges are pulled apart, and it is opened so the viewer can see the woven interior before the segment ends.

action.detailed: Weave the black, red, and white paper layers together, fold them into a pocket, flip the pocket over, and open it to display the interior.

nodes.plm_action: showcasing the wallet from different angles
nodes.plm_caption: This video captures a time lapsed sequence of someone demonstrating a wallet made out of duct tape and cardboard. It starts with the man holding two pieces of the wallet open, then the man shows both halves and makes them go in and out. Then the man starts to make a basket by closing and opening half the wallet with his hand and placing a piece of cardboard down. The man closes the wallet, opens it, puts another piece of cardboard in it, and closes it. Then, the man shows the wallet with both hands at two sides, opens it to show both hands inside, then closes it and shows the inside and outside, opens the wallet again, to show the entire wallet, the man opens it again and the basket is almost ready. Then, the man holds up the basket fully opened, and then closes it, and finally, the man shows the wallet opened and closed. The wallet is set against a yellow table with a graph design.

summary.brief: A time‑lapse shows hands assembling a duct‑tape wallet on a yellow‑grid table.
summary.detailed: The clip begins with a pair of hands holding the two halves of a duct‑tape wallet open and moving them apart and together. The maker then folds one half around a piece of cardboard, closes the wallet, reopens it, places another cardboard insert, and closes it again, gradually forming a basket‑like shape. The hands repeatedly open and close the wallet to display both the interior and exterior, holding the wallet from opposite sides to show the inside space, then opening it fully to reveal the whole structure. Finally, the assembled basket is held up fully opened, closed once more, and the wallet is presented one last time opened and closed, all set against a yellow table with a graph paper pattern.

action.detailed: Using both hands, fold the duct‑tape halves around cardboard pieces, repeatedly open and close them to shape a basket‑like wallet, and display the interior and exterior of the completed piece.

nodes.plm_action: Cut red, black, and white duct tape into strips
nodes.plm_caption: This video features a time-lapse of a pair of hands cutting and folding tape into a striped pattern.

summary.brief: Cutting, folding, and applying colored duct‑tape strips to a paper base.
summary.detailed: The maker first places rolls of red, white and black duct tape on a yellow‑gridded cutting mat and positions a metal ruler for measurement. Using a pen knife, short lengths of each colored tape are marked and cut, then each strip is folded lengthwise to form narrow ribbons. The folded ribbons are laid out side‑by‑side on the mat, spaced with the ruler. A small piece of red paper is then positioned on the mat; a black tape strip is adhered to its corner, followed by white and red strips that are pressed onto the paper, flipped, and excess tape trimmed. Additional colored paper strips are added and taped together, creating a layered arrangement of red, black and white pieces on the work surface.

action.detailed: Cut short lengths of colored duct tape, fold each piece lengthwise, then press the folded strips onto the paper, layering the colors to build the design.

nodes.plm_action: Get a double sided tape and place on top of the bag
nodes.plm_caption:
A person is demonstrating how to cut and make some art with tape. You can see a hand in the back that helps the person cut the tape. The tape is red, black, and white, and is on a yellow background. The video is at a quick pace. The art made with the tape looks like a guitar keyboard.
The person has a hand in the background to help them cut the tape. The yellow background helps with visibility. The tape is red, black, and white, with the colors layered at the front. The art piece looks like a guitar keyboard.

summary.brief: A hand places a red tape strip onto a black‑white striped pattern on a yellow grid mat.
summary.detailed: In a close‑up view, the demonstrator’s right hand lifts a red strip of duct tape, flips it over and moves it above a row of black and white tape strips that have already been arranged on a yellow, grid‑lined cutting mat. The hand aligns the red strip with the existing pieces, presses it down at the edge of the layout, and secures it, extending the alternating colour pattern that resembles a keyboard. Clear nail polish can be seen on the fingertips, and bright lighting highlights the vivid red, black and white colors against the yellow background.

action.detailed: Place the red tape strip onto the existing black‑and‑white striped layout, align it with the other strips, and press it firmly into position.

nodes.plm_action: Weave tape strips together in intricate patterns to form base of tablecloth
nodes.plm_caption: The video features someone attaching four strips of different colored duct tape in order to make a piece of striped art. The person is seen applying red, black, white, and black strips from their right to their left, one at a time, before flipping the completed strip to display it. The same process is repeated, and another strip is added to the front of the last completed strip, then flipped to show it all the way around. The person then adds two more strips, ends up with eight strips that are now lined up. At the end of the video, the person holds a long black strip from their right and moves it to their left to add it to the completed artwork. A yellow background with grids is used for the art to be made and displayed on.

summary.brief: Hands assemble red, black and white duct‑tape strips on a yellow‑grid mat, repeatedly adding and flipping layers until a multi‑strip stack is finished and a final black strip is slid into place.
summary.detailed: The creator first tears a red duct‑tape strip in half with the right hand while the left hand pins black and white strips onto a black backing placed on a yellow‑checkered cutting mat. A long red strip is then pulled together and laid beside the existing black and white pieces, followed by additional red, black and white pieces that are folded or stacked in a right‑to‑left order. After a few layers are arranged, the partially built bundle is flipped over to expose its other side, and the same color sequence is added again, extending the strip. This add‑and‑flip routine continues until eight strips are aligned side‑by‑side, forming a continuous multi‑color strip. Finally, a longer black strip is lifted from the right edge and slid leftward onto the completed stack, where it is pressed into place to secure the finished tape artwork.

action.detailed: Place a torn red strip, then layer black, white, and another black strip on the mat, flip the partial bundle, repeat the layering sequence until eight strips are aligned, and finally slide a long black strip from the right onto the finished stack, pressing it into place.

nodes.plm_action: Weave duct tape together in a crisscross pattern
nodes.plm_caption: The video is an instructional video demonstrating how to make a weave using craft tape. The weave is black and red and white tape cut into squares. The person doing the weaving is using both hands. The tape has been cut with the square sides facing up and down and facing left and right, making the weaving task easier. The person is showing the audience how to weave by using their hands. A cut, grey plastic ruler is visible on the work surface. The background work surface is a pale yellow, self-healing cutting mat with grid lines. A shadow of the person can be seen.

summary.brief: The maker weaves red, white and black tape squares into a tri‑weave pattern on a yellow cutting mat and then flips the finished piece.
summary.detailed: Starting with pre‑cut red, white and black tape squares laid out on a pale‑yellow self‑healing cutting mat, the presenter uses both hands to interlace the squares in an over‑under sequence, aligning each piece with the nearby grey ruler so that a tri‑weave texture builds across the mat. The rapid weaving continues until most of the area is filled. Near the end the partially completed weave is lifted, the edges are adjusted, the piece is turned over, and the hands reposition it while the camera pans to show the completed design.

action.detailed: Using both hands, alternately place each red, white, or black tape square over and under the existing rows on the cutting mat, aligning them with the ruler to create the tri‑weave pattern, then lift, smooth and flip the finished piece for display.

nodes.plm_action: Anchoring the first row with pinching tape using 1-inch increments
nodes.plm_caption: The video shows a person's fingers inspecting and adjusting a black and red woven cloth. The fabric is on top of a measuring board with grid lines. Only the person's hands are visible. There is a pen lying on top of the board near the fabric.

summary.brief: Hands adjust a woven black‑red‑white strip on a grid‑marked board.
summary.detailed: The camera stays fixed on a measuring board that has visible grid lines while only the demonstrator’s hands are shown. Fingertips lift, slide, and smooth a woven strip of black, red and white material, inspecting the alignment and nudging sections until the colored pieces sit evenly together. A pen lies nearby on the board, but no other objects or people appear.

action.detailed: Lift the woven strip with your fingertips, slide it into position, and smooth the pattern until the black, red, and white sections line up evenly on the board.

nodes.plm_action: Cut two lines at about one-inch marks
nodes.plm_caption: This video features an upward panning shot of an intricate wallet with various shapes and a design of red, white and black tape being worked on by two hands using a precision knife on a cutting mat. Then a set of hands uses a ruler to align and press the design onto the wallet. The wallet is then placed in between the two hands who press it open and closed, to show off the finished design. All of this is observed at a slow speed.

summary.brief: The maker cuts, aligns, and presses red, white, and black tape onto a woven wallet and then opens and closes it to display the finished tri‑weave design.
summary.detailed: Two hands use a precision knife on a yellow cutting mat to trim strips of red, white, and black duct tape, then place a ruler to line the pieces and press the tape onto the surface of the intricate woven wallet. After the patterned tape is applied, the hands lift the wallet, slowly open it, flip it around, and close it again, showing the interior pockets and the completed tri‑weave texture from several angles.

action.detailed: Cut the colored tape with a precision knife, align the strips using a ruler, press them onto the woven wallet, then open, flip, and close the wallet to showcase its finished design.

nodes.plm_action: Holding the final piece to show it off
nodes.plm_caption: A woman points to a white and red design on a black background while holding it with her left hand. Then, the design is on its own, folding in half.

summary.brief: A woman points to a white‑and‑red pattern on a black wallet and then folds the wallet in half.
summary.detailed: On a yellow‑grid tabletop the creator holds the partially‑finished black duct‑tape wallet with her left hand, counts the alternating red, black and white squares using her left and right pointer fingers, then uses her right index finger to highlight a white‑and‑red design on the wallet’s surface. After displaying the design, she folds the wallet neatly in half and places the folded piece back onto the mat.

action.detailed: Point to the white‑and‑red design with your right index finger while gripping the black wallet with your left hand, then fold the wallet in half.

nodes.plm_caption: A human hand is showing a collection of different styles of cloth wristbands. Some of the wristbands have colorful patches or designs. Both pieces are rotated and flipped so their front and back faces can be seen, and the demonstrator briefly twists the two fragments together to form a circular shape before setting them down. summary.brief: Hands interlace red, black and white duct‑tape strips on a yellow grid mat.

summary.brief: The maker cuts multicolored duct‑tape strips and folds each strip in half on a grid‑lined measuring mat.
summary.detailed: First, a metal ruler is placed against a piece of red, black and white duct tape and a sharp knife slices the tape into short strips; the hand holds each strip against the ruler while cutting. action.detailed: Fold each red, black, and white duct‑tape strip in half by gripping its ends with the left and right hands, bringing the ends together while flipping the strip, and aligning the folded strips in a row on the grid‑lined mat.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: How To Make A Duct Tape Tri-Weave Wallet!!
summary_sent_to_llm.description: Hope you enjoyed and check back next Wednesday for weaving Wednesday!!
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video begins with the presenter greeting viewers for “Weaving Wednesday” and listing the supplies: three colors of duct tape, a metal ruler, an X‑Acto knife, and clear tape. Strips of each color are measured and cut – 8‑inch pieces are halved and then each half is folded back on itself to make a rounded edge, while a 9‑inch length is cut into thirds for each color and then each third is halved and folded the same way. An 8‑inch strip designated as the trim is also cut in half. The folded 3‑inch strips are aligned on a yellow grid mat and attached to the trim piece at about a quarter‑inch interval, forming a base strip. The presenter then weaves the three colors together by laying the first color over one strip, under the next, and repeating this over‑under pattern across the whole length; the second and third colors are woven in the same alternating fashion, creating the tri‑color effect. After the weave is complete, clear tape is applied to the back, and the sides are taped along the top edge. The excess edge is trimmed with a ruler to about a quarter of an inch, then folded inward so the woven panel has a rounded outer edge.
